reason: I'll start with the warm response by following the nerve signals to the skin vessels.
expectation: I expect the skin vessels to widen, increasing heat transfer to the cooler air.

alternatives.reason: Sweating also helps oppose warming, but I'll examine blood flow first.

effect: The widened vessels carry more blood to the skin, where heat moves to the cooler surroundings. I'll continue the warm response.
reaction: The heat arrows make the role of increased skin blood flow clear.
reason: Sweat glands are the other warm-condition target, so I'll follow that response next.
expectation: I expect nerve signals to stimulate sweating, which may cool the skin as water evaporates.

alternatives.reason: The cold response would provide a useful contrast, but I'll finish exploring warmth first.

effect: The signal produces liquid sweat, so evaporation remains to be shown.
reaction: Separating sweating from evaporation makes the cooling mechanism clearer.
reason: I'll expose the sweat to air to follow the warm response through to cooling.
expectation: I expect some sweat to evaporate and carry heat away from the skin.

alternatives.reason: Cold-condition vessel changes would contrast with warming, but I'll finish the sweat pathway first.

effect: Evaporation removes heat and the temperature moves toward its earlier range; humid air reduces evaporation. The warm goal is complete, so I'll turn to cooling.
reaction: The distinction between producing sweat and evaporating it is useful.
reason: I'll compare the cold response of skin vessels with their widening in warmth.
expectation: I expect the vessels to narrow, reducing blood flow near the surface and heat loss.

alternatives.reason: Muscle activity may produce heat, but the vessel response provides a direct comparison first.

effect: Vessel narrowing reduces heat loss without producing heat; the remaining action addresses muscle.
reaction: The distinction between conserving and producing heat is clear.
reason: I'll follow the only available combination to complete the cold response.
expectation: I expect muscle contractions to produce heat, perhaps through shivering.

effect: Shivering uses ATP and produces heat, complementing the reduced heat loss from narrowed skin vessels; the cold goal is complete.
reaction: The contrast between producing and conserving heat was clear and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following sweat from liquid droplets to evaporation was most worthwhile: it distinguished sweat production from actual cooling and showed why humid air reduces evaporation.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sweat-gland step alone felt somewhat incomplete, although the subsequent evaporation step made its purpose clear.

surprise.text: The humid-air comparison usefully showed that sweating does not guarantee the same amount of cooling.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the vessel and muscle actions had clear, contrasting purposes. The compatible menu supplied the available pairings rather than requiring me to discover them.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue for more comparisons linking familiar body responses to their mechanisms, especially when the picture plans distinguish easily confused processes.
